method: The report is read by a strict XML reader built into the page. Each <testcase> element counts once. Its status comes from its child elements: a <failure> child makes it a failure, an <error> child makes it an error, a <skipped> child makes it skipped, and a test case with none of those children passes. When a test case carries more than one of those children the precedence is failure, then error, then skipped, so a test case that was both skipped and failed is reported as a failure. The pass count is the total number of test cases minus the failures, errors and skips. A test case is attributed to the nearest enclosing <testsuite>, so a suite row counts only the test cases directly inside it and the rows of a report with nested suites do not add up to the file total. Each suite row also shows the suite time attribute when it has one, and otherwise the sum of its own test case times. The report duration is the sum of the suite time attributes when every suite carries a numeric time, otherwise the sum of every test case time, otherwise it is reported as having no timing attributes. Declared attributes are not trusted: the tests attributes are summed and compared with the counted <testcase> elements, and a difference is shown as a warning instead of replacing the counted total. Numeric attributes must be a non-negative decimal; a time that does not match is ignored rather than guessed at. The slowest list holds the five test cases with the largest time values, ties kept in document order, and only the first 50 failing test cases are listed with their type, message and the first line of the failure text. The reader rejects what it cannot read exactly: a DOCTYPE declaration, an unknown entity, a repeated attribute, a malformed or unclosed tag, more than one root element, text outside the root, more than 200000 elements or more than 4000000 characters. The root element must be <testsuites> or <testsuite>, element names may carry a namespace prefix, and element and attribute names are matched by their local name. Names and messages are whitespace-collapsed and truncated at 140, 240, 240 and 80 characters respectively for display. No validation harness is run, no test is re-executed and nothing is uploaded: the file is parsed as text in the browser tab with no network access, accounts or storage.

sources.title: JUnit XML report format as emitted by pytest, Maven Surefire, Gradle, Jest and gotestsum: testsuites and testsuite elements carrying tests, failures, errors and time attributes, with testcase children.
XML 1.0 specification: element and attribute syntax, quoted attribute values, the five predefined entities and numeric character references.
XSD schema for the common JUnit report format: testcase elements carry name, classname and time, and failure, error and skipped are child elements.
